newsitem.title: POLAND: Prime minister braces Poland for more floods.
newsitem.headline: Prime minister braces Poland for more floods.

text.p: Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz braced his country on Friday for more flooding this weekend, saying the government would do all it could to compensate victims.
"We have to go forward, we have to think about in what way we can remove the effects of the cataclysm," Cimoszewicz said in a televised address after the evening news.
"On the proposal of the government, more than 30 laws have been amended -- all so that aid should reach you quickly and without unnecessary bureaucratic procedures," he said.

Parliament adopted emergency legislation on Thursday night to allow the government to increase borrowing and to rush funds and aid to stricken areas. President Aleksander Kwasniewski announced early on Friday he had signed the legislative amendments into law.
Parliament also hastily amended the communist-era state of emergency law so it could be applied in case of further floods.

On Friday evening Kwasniewski, visiting flooded areas in the southeastern Tarnobrzeg province, said he would sign the amended law but for the time being had no intention of calling a state of emergency, PAP news agency reported.
He said earlier in the day that a declaration of a state of emergency would delay parliamentary elections due on September 21.
Poland's official crisis committee said that more floods were on the way after steady rainfall throughout Friday on the western third of the country already mourning 48 deaths in the two-week crisis.
Committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes said the effects of the rainfall would be evident in the next few hours.
Pomes said the rain was lighter than downpours two weeks ago, but the ground was saturated and reservoirs full.
